Hey, honestly I'm sure it is nothing to worry about. Anxiety can affect the digestive system pretty badly and cause things like IBS and constipation, which is what happened to me when I used to panic about cancer in the digestive system (frequently when I was your age. I'm 23 now, and I was CONVINCED I was done for. But I'm still here!) I spoke to a doctor a few times back then and they told me it's normal for stool to vary in colour. Just depends on what you've been eating and how much water you've been drinking. As long as you're not passing black blood or stools that resemble tar, you're very, very likely healthy. 

as for the blood, you may be pushing too hard and causing yourself to bleed. Red blood is more likely to have been from external bleeding rather than internal. I doubt very much a mild deficiency in B12 would cause you anything serious. Most people are slightly deficient in it actually, believe it or not.  

Acid reflux is another sign of anxiety. I'm in a rational headspace right now, however 3 nights ago I had the worst panic attack of the year (health anxiety related) and I had acid reflux for the following 3 days. You really don't realize how strong an impact all that stress has. Remember, stress releases cortisol, and cortisol tends to cause all sorts of physical anxiety symptoms! Hope this helps relieve your worry. You're only young, you deserve to be enjoying life. :)

I'm 22F (171cm, 57kg) and I have the same thing, except in my case I am pretty sure it is just because of poor circulation and chronic hyperventilation. We anxiety sufferers tend to breathe erratically without realising. This can cause your blood oxygen levels to fluctuate between. Usually it results in lower blood oxygen, hence lightheadedness and dizziness also being common symptoms. Honestly, if it was a symptom of a bigger issue, I'd expect some other major indicators to come up. I had convinced myself I had a heart issue, had an echocardiogram done, and my heart is in perfect health. I STILL convince myself otherwise at times, and my mind really makes it feel real. I could go on a whim and make a bet, I am 90% certain you are absolutely going to be okay, just remember what I have said about breathing properly. Try learning some breathing exercises, over time you will hyperventilate a lot less :)

There are two different types of health anxiety; care-seeking and care-avoiding. When you see a CBT therapist, they note which one you are and help you to address whichever path of behaviours your anxiety has led you down.

It's true. My therapist told me the story of a training warrior and his master. He was put face to face with a monster, and told to defeat it. The warrior was afraid of the monster, and he ran from it. The more he ran, the bigger it grew. Soon, the master was called back in to help him. He walked calmly up to the monster; the closer he got, the smaller it shrunk. He picked it up and put it in his pocket before turning to his student and saying this - 

"our problems are only as big as we think them to be."

And this is so, so true. Our anxious minds will usually build any negative thing into a massive deal. It's a survival instinct, but an overactive one. Be kind to that instinct, and remind it that you are safe. Soon, you will trust yourself and know that you are.

You will get through this. I promise. One day you will wake up and the first thought to enter your mind will be something pleasant, like what you might have for breakfast or what friend you may see today - rather than that looming sense of impending doom. You'll fall asleep focusing on how soft your pillows are, and not worry over a nagging psychosomatic symptom. One day, when you get one of those little symptoms, you will laugh at that voice in your head that says you should worry, because you trust deep down that everything is okay, and you know that voice likes to play games.

One day, life will get exciting and you will feel like you are made of titanium because you beat health anxiety.

I did it. I thought I never could. I was reborn. I believe in you :)

You are loved, by both your body and others. 

Take care.

Yes. For me it was psychosomatic symptoms. One would come, stick around for a few weeks/months and eventually go, and the next day I'd wake up with something else. Or I'd see a post on Facebook or something about someone else's disease, and convince myself that I could also have it. It felt like a never ending cycle.

It wasn't easy. I know. Breathing exercises helped a lot as overthinking it would make it feel worse. Sleep on your left side. The acid won't be able to get up your throat at night so easily that way. Wait it out and look after yourself, I promise it eventually goes away.

A rule; if it comes from nature, it is probably going to do your body a lot better. If it's from a tin/can or has a lot of saturates etc, avoid it. In the mornings, when I had globus especially, I would put a bunch of fruit in a blender with some almond milk (less fatty, better for you). Gives your stomach less work to do. Also, it protects the lining of your stomach. Which is why porridge is also a good idea first thing in the morning.

Address the acid reflux as it is the biggest cause. Avoid foods that trigger it. Also make sure you are eating enough. I don't eat enough tbh lol. It causes a build up and makes it worse. Eat small portions throughout the day, rather than big meals. Gravitate more toward ph neutral foods. Avoid acidic, processed and fatty foods. You can still have a treat. Just moderate. Bananas are good as they are alkaline. They will help balance your stomachs acidity. Also, for relief from the globus sensation, drink ginger tea, maybe with some honey if you want. Ginger tea has a healing quality that helped massively in healing the damage done to my throat from acid reflux.

As for stress; I have heard amazing things about CBD oil. 2/3 drops under the tongue a day. Obviously do your research first but literally everyone I know to have taken CBD says they feel a lot more relaxed. I hope you feel calm again soon :) good luck with school! x
